name: DAILOQ
line: An AI chat assistant for WhatsApp, Instagram and Telegram
headline: An AI customer-messaging assistant built for Azerbaijan
subtitle: One assistant across Telegram, Instagram, WhatsApp and the web — it answers from your documents, takes actions and hands hard questions to a human.
overview: Dailoq is an AI assistant for customer conversations, built for businesses in Azerbaijan. Whichever channel a customer writes from — Telegram, Instagram, WhatsApp or a website widget — the same assistant answers, in Azerbaijani, Russian or English. It works from the company's own documents, carries out simple tasks such as booking a table, and passes difficult conversations to a human operator with a summary.
problem: Small and mid-sized businesses answer the same questions in several messengers by hand, often out of hours and in a mix of Azerbaijani and Russian. Global chatbot platforms don't understand local dialects, letter substitutions or mixed-language messages, price in foreign currency and tend to invent an answer when they don't know one.
approach: We built the assistant around the local language first: Azerbaijani — with dialect phrases, letter substitutions and mixed AZ–RU sentences — is tested on its own. Answers are retrieved from the client's files and every reply shows its source; when the assistant can't confirm something it says so and offers a human. Every change to the bot's brain has to pass an evaluation set before it reaches customers.
result: More than 15 companies use Dailoq. They get one assistant for every channel that answers from their own documents — around 98% of answers are correct, with at most 2% errors — understands voice messages and photos, books and confirms actions and hands over to operators with full context, all managed from a single no-code panel with conversation history and monthly reports.

features.d: Telegram, Instagram, WhatsApp and a web widget all work, the Meta channels through Meta's official integration. The conversation carries on when a customer switches channels.
Understands dialect, letter substitutions and mixed AZ–RU–EN messages, and replies in the customer's language.
Searches PDF, DOCX, XLSX, TXT, Markdown, URLs and FAQs by meaning; every answer shows the file it came from, and unanswered questions become FAQ entries in one click.
The same multimodal model understands voice messages and photos — a menu, for example — and answers from them, with no separate OCR step.
Asks for confirmation, then books a table or calls the client's own system through a REST connector — with an idempotency key, so nothing runs twice.
Hard questions go to an operator with a short summary; owners manage tone, knowledge, channels, team roles and history from one no-code panel.

architecture.d: A growing set of real questions — about half in Azerbaijani, 30% Russian, 20% English — runs on every change; if the score drops, the release is blocked.

Role-based access plus database-level isolation keep each client's data apart; connection keys are stored encrypted and an append-only audit log records every action. Production runs on a Contabo server in Europe behind Cloudflare.

Adapters for several AI models, and a routing layer that picks the model for each request — switching provider is a configuration change, not a rewrite. Embeddings come from a self-hosted bge-m3 model, and semantic search runs inside PostgreSQL with pgvector.

v: Multimodal model for voice and images

name: CHEFMARKET
headline: A restaurant–supplier B2B marketplace ecosystem
subtitle: Three mobile apps, an admin panel and a real-time backend — in one ecosystem.
overview: ChefMarket fully digitises restaurant–supplier trade in Azerbaijan: suppliers sell products, restaurants place orders and drivers deliver. Three separate mobile apps (Supplier, Restaurant, Driver), a React admin panel and a Tenant Portal talk to each other in real time through a single .NET 8 backend.
problem: Restaurant supply ran on phone calls, WhatsApp and paper delivery notes. Nobody knew exactly where an order was, prices could not be compared, and the cash a driver collected was reconciled by hand at the end of the day.
approach: Every role got its own app — one each for suppliers, restaurants and drivers — with an admin panel on top. The whole order lifecycle sits on one status flow, pushed to all three parties at the same moment over SignalR. When the network drops, actions go into an offline queue and are replayed on reconnect.
result: Orders, delivery and cash reconciliation now live in one panel. Suppliers manage their own catalogue through Buy Box competition and bulk price updates, and restaurants collect quotes from several suppliers at once with a tender request.

features.d: Accepted → preparing → ready → on the way, with a real-time notification at every step.
Market price comparison and recommendations for the supplier.
A restaurant asks once and collects prices from many suppliers.
Waves, routes and stops, plus driver assignment.
Expected versus collected cash, tracked per stop.
Actions are kept when the network drops and replayed when it returns.

architecture.d: A single SignalR toast bridge with map-based dedup (a 500ms window) stops the same event being shown twice.
Backend PascalCase becomes camelCase at the service boundary, so components never deal with two naming schemes.
The database holds only relative paths and IStorageUrlResolver builds the full address, so moving storage never touches the data.

headline: A multi-tenant SaaS for door and window manufacturers

overview: Vicdoor replaces the Excel-based workflow in a PVC and aluminium door and window manufacturer’s workshops with one integrated digital system. It covers quoting, visual design, production, field installation and customer satisfaction, and is tailored to the Baku market.
problem: Workshops priced jobs in Excel, wrote measurements on paper and checked production status by phone. Finding the state of one order meant calling three people, and the same data lived in three different places.
approach: The whole order lifecycle runs through a single status workflow with an audit trail. The price calculator, visual designer and drawing engine are shared packages used by web, mobile and API alike. An offline-first mobile app serves field installers, with measurements without internet, annotations on images and digital signatures.
result: Manual hand-offs between quoting and production are gone. The designer exports PDF and DXF files straight to CNC machines, and customers get a magic-link portal with live production status and a warranty card.

features.d: Profile systems, glass packages, steel frames and accessories, with multi-currency maths under VAT and central-bank exchange rates.
Geometric constraint solving and CNC-ready PDF and DXF export.
Measuring, annotation, signatures and on-site pricing without a connection.
A workshop kiosk, a TV status panel and cut optimisation.
Quotes, live status and a warranty card behind a magic link.
Invoicing, payment reconciliation, P&L including COGS, and real-time stock.

architecture.d: PostgreSQL Row-Level Security keeps every tenant’s data separate.
tRPC v11 with shared Zod contracts across web, mobile and API.
PDF and DXF generation, cron tasks and push notifications run on BullMQ and Redis workers.

name: ALTISCASSA
line: An integrated finance and cash management platform
headline: An integrated finance and cash management platform
subtitle: Multi-currency cash management, counterparty debts and 11+ financial reports.
overview: AltisCassa is an all-in-one system that centralises a business’s cash operations, counterparty obligations, project budgets and corporate reporting, handling multi-currency transactions, invoice flows and financial reports in real time.
problem: Cash, debts and project budgets were kept in separate Excel files. Month-end profit and loss meant merging them by hand, and nobody had a clear real-time balance per currency.
approach: Clean Architecture with separate domain, application, infrastructure and API layers. Every operation leaves an audit trail, and deletions are soft-only, so financial data is never lost for good.
result: Profit and loss, cash flow, turnover, VAT and ageing reports are generated instantly, and a Ctrl+K command palette gives one-step access to the advanced features.

features.d: Cash across multiple currencies in one place.
Debt management with per-currency analytics.
Budget versus actual spending and profitability analysis.
From draft to payment, including printing.
Jump to any advanced feature in one step.

architecture.d: Domain, application, infrastructure and API layers kept strictly apart.
Every operation is recorded and nothing financial is ever permanently deleted.

name: E-HESAB
headline: An AI-based pre-accounting platform
subtitle: DVX integration, OCR invoices and a dynamic tax engine.
overview: e-Hesab is a mobile-first, AI-driven pre-accounting platform for freelancers and small and medium businesses. It is localised to Azerbaijani tax law and the State Tax Service infrastructure, and automates invoices, expense tracking, payroll, DSMF and e-Qaimə processes.
problem: Freelancers and small businesses often learn their tax obligations at the last moment. Receipts stay on paper, expenses go untracked and filing deadlines are forgotten — and an accountant is too expensive at this scale.
approach: Tax calculations are not hardcoded. Simplified tax, VAT, profit tax and payroll deductions run on a configurable dynamic engine, so nobody rewrites code when legislation changes. Paper documents become digital invoices through camera capture, OCR and the Claude API.
result: Users see their tax calendar, expected payments and potential penalties in advance. e-Qaiməs go straight to the DVX portal, and expenses entered offline sync when the network returns.

features.d: Photograph a paper receipt and turn it into a digital invoice.
Submit declarations and send XML-based e-receipts automatically.
Rates are changed through configuration, not code.
Assigns expenses to ledger accounts and recommends month-end closing steps.
Tracks deadlines, calculates penalties and sends timely push notifications.

architecture.d: Isolated domains with CQRS and MediatR that could later be split into microservices.
Expenses and invoices are saved locally in SQLite and synced to the central server when connectivity returns.
Sign-in through ASAN Login with JWT-based authentication.

name: E-FAKTURA
line: An offline invoicing app for small business
headline: An offline invoicing app for small business
subtitle: An invoicing solution that works without internet, fully in Azerbaijani.
overview: E-Faktura is an offline-first mobile app for entrepreneurs and freelancers. It covers A4 invoice creation, client management and payment tracking. Data stays on the device, and invoices can be sent as PDF or over WhatsApp.
problem: Small business owners either write invoices in Word templates or do not issue them at all, and cloud tools fail wherever there is no internet.
approach: The app is built offline-first on local SQLite storage with no server. The code is split into layers — repository, pure business logic, state, UI — and the calculation logic is covered by unit tests.
result: Users can issue invoices offline, track debts, send WhatsApp deep-link payment reminders and scan paper invoices with the camera.

features.d: Five templates, adjustable tax rate, multi-line items and currency support.
Partial and full payments, unpaid / paid / overdue statuses and a receivables and payables balance.
Scan a paper invoice with the camera.
With Azerbaijani phone-number normalisation.
Export and import the data on the device.

architecture.d: Repository → pure business logic → state → UI.
The calculation core is unit-tested and the codebase runs in TypeScript strict mode.

Finance, progress and efficiency reports.
Planned versus actual.
Budget overruns, safety incidents and delays.

The office and the site work from the same data.
Managers, contractors and owners each see what they need.

Shipping rules, the equipment fleet and corporate information in one platform.

name: NITRO GARAGE
line: A car service and spare parts marketplace
headline: An automotive service and spare parts marketplace
subtitle: Driver, mechanic and store on one platform — four roles, 79+ screens.
overview: Nitro Garage is a mobile app digitising Azerbaijan’s car service market. It connects drivers, mechanics and spare-parts stores on one platform: drivers post service or part requests, and mechanics and stores send real-time bids so the cheapest option can be chosen.
problem: Drivers call stores one by one to compare part prices, do not know a mechanic’s workload, and struggle to find help when stranded. The market lacks price transparency.
approach: A tender model — one request, many offers. Separate navigators and screen sets were built for four roles: driver, mechanic, store and admin. A geolocation-based SOS flow covers emergencies.
result: Drivers get several offers from one request and compare prices. Stores sell inventory with auto-bid rules, and mechanics manage their bookings through the app.

features.d: Drivers post requests; mechanics and stores bid.
Nearby mechanics are alerted automatically using geolocation.
Camera and OCR identify the vehicle.
Diagnostics plus service and part recommendations.
Transaction history, refunds and per-role balances.

architecture.d: Fully separate navigators and screens for each role.
Each backend domain has its own service layer, all going through one central axios client with JWT injection and token refresh.
Zustand stores for cross-screen state, useState for local state — Redux deliberately not used.

name: JOBREMOTELY
headline: A curated remote job board
subtitle: Vacancies with publicly disclosed salaries, verified by HR and free of spam.
overview: JobRemotely is a job board that brings together HR-verified vacancies for remote engineers, designers and operators. It publishes only remote roles with disclosed salaries and moves candidates from application to offer through an automated flow.
problem: Remote job seekers get lost among spam listings, hidden salaries and recruiter messages. After applying, candidates never know which stage their application is in.
approach: Vacancies are collected by scheduled scraping of the Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby ATS platforms, then filtered by salary and language. Application status is bound to a finite state machine: it changes only through permitted transitions, so candidates always see the right stage.
result: Candidates apply with one click and move transparently through skills testing, language verification, interviews and the offer stage. Admins see live funnel, throughput and stage-time metrics.

features.d: HR-verified, spam-free remote vacancies. Companies cannot see applicant identities (blind apply).
Application → screening → skills test → language → interview → offer → hiring.
Auto-fill a profile from a CV and generate cover letters.
Scheduled collection from ATS platforms with salary and language filters.
Funnel, throughput and stage-time metrics calculated from status events.

architecture.d: Application status changes only through allowed transitions; optimistic-concurrency conflicts are guarded with HTTP 409.
Zod schemas are shared between API and frontend, and responses use typed ok() / err() envelopes.
Email, scraping, Telegram notifications and view counters run in a pg-boss worker outside the web process.

v: OpenAI — CV-based profile filling and cover letters

name: MOLEAKS
headline: A leaked-data search platform
subtitle: Deep search by email, phone number, domain and face recognition.
chips: 4 search vectors — email, phone, domain, face
SSR fast, SEO-friendly UI on Next.js

metrics.l: search vectors — email, phone, domain, face

overview: Moleaks is a verification tool for individuals and cybersecurity specialists. It shows whether their data appears in leaked databases on the internet or the dark web — an email address, a mobile number, a domain name or a face can be checked.
problem: People often learn that their data has leaked only after an account is compromised. Leak databases are scattered, unformatted and hold millions of rows, which makes manual checking impossible.
approach: Search and analysis are separated. A .NET Core API handles thousands of simultaneous requests while heavy analysis runs in the background with Python and DeepScanner. Database indexing strategies let millions of rows be scanned in seconds.
result: Users can check an email, a phone number or a whole corporate domain and get a detailed report on the leak’s source, date and type.

features.d: Fast checks across leaked databases by email, mobile number and IP address.
Finds leaked accounts tied to a corporate or personal domain.
Identifies people in internet images by facial features.
Automated analysis of large volumes of leaked data.
Detailed reports on each leak’s source, date and type.

architecture.d: Python and DeepScanner run in the background, so large analyses never slow the main system.
MSSQL indexing lets millions of rows be scanned in seconds.
.NET Core securely handles thousands of concurrent search requests.

v: MS SQL Server with indexing strategies

name: SAFEMOLE
line: A digital security and privacy platform
headline: A digital security and privacy platform
subtitle: Fully native iOS and Android, a hybrid database and end-to-end encryption.
chips: 2 fully native apps — Kotlin and Swift
2 databases — MSSQL for ACID, MongoDB for logs

metrics.l: fully native apps — Kotlin and Swift

overview: Safemole is a native mobile solution for protecting personal and corporate data, managing it securely and keeping detailed records. The iOS and Android apps are both fully native, which gives direct access to device security features such as biometrics and the secure enclave.
problem: Privacy apps are usually built cross-platform, which limits access to the device’s security hardware. Logging every security event also bloats the main database and slows the system down.
approach: Each platform is built in its own native language — Kotlin for Android, Swift for iOS. The database is polyglot: transactional data sits in MSSQL under ACID guarantees, while continuous operational logs are written to MongoDB, so the main database stays fast.
result: Logins and every sensitive operation are verified with hardware-level biometrics. When a suspicious login attempt or unauthorised data export happens, the user gets an immediate push notification.

features.d: Optimal use of device resources, high speed and a polished UI.
Real-time records of every step, API request and security event.
Hardware-level verification via FaceID, TouchID and the Android Fingerprint API.
Sensitive data is protected in transit and at rest.
Immediate push notifications for suspicious logins or unauthorised data extraction.

architecture.d: Transactional data in MSSQL with ACID guarantees, continuous logs in MongoDB — the core database never slows down.
MVVM or VIPER on mobile and a modular backend, with business logic, data layer and UI clearly separated.
Every request passes through a single gateway with a firewall and rate limiting.

name: RANA
line: A digital legacy and message-to-the-future platform
headline: A digital legacy and message-to-the-future platform
subtitle: A time capsule where encrypted messages open only on a scheduled date.
chips: E2E end-to-end encryption — invisible even to admins

metrics.l: end-to-end encryption — invisible even to admins

overview: Rana is a time-capsule solution that securely delivers memories, important messages and digital legacy to future generations. Users schedule messages for family members years ahead; the data is encrypted and opens only on a predetermined date, for the chosen heirs.
problem: Digital legacy — passwords, documents, family videos — is usually not organised anywhere. Storing it in the cloud means the provider or an administrator could, in principle, read it.
approach: Content is end-to-end encrypted, so no third party, administrators included, can reach videos or messages. Large video and audio files are stored asynchronously in encrypted cloud storage to keep the database light, and the backend is set up for high availability with Docker and Nginx.
result: A user can schedule a video message, a document or a will for their child’s 18th birthday. When the time comes, the recipient is notified by SMS, email or push notification, and the content opens only at that moment.

features.d: Schedule text, voice or video messages for a specific future date and time.
Store documents, passwords and wills securely and pass them to heirs when the time comes.
Recipients are notified at the scheduled time by SMS, email or push.
A refined, minimalist interface with navigation suited to every age group.

architecture.d: Custom cryptography, so no third party — the administrator included — can access content.
Large video and audio files are stored asynchronously in encrypted cloud storage.
The backend is isolated with Docker and set up for high availability behind an Nginx reverse proxy.

v: Cloud storage (AWS S3 or Azure Blob) for encrypted files

name: GURABA
line: A global e-commerce and sales ecosystem
headline: A global e-commerce and sales ecosystem

overview: Guraba is more than a standard e-commerce site. It combines a website, a mobile app and a Telegram bot into one multi-channel sales ecosystem. problem: A customer fills a cart on the site, asks questions on Telegram, then downloads the app — and has to start over on every channel. The store owner has to sit at a computer to approve orders.
approach: All channels sit on a single API, so accounts and carts are identical across web, mobile and the bot. The database is hybrid: financial transactions and stock live in MSSQL with ACID guarantees, while thousands of clicks and logs per second are written asynchronously to MongoDB.
result: Stock changes reach every channel within milliseconds and are pushed to the admin app. The store owner approves orders from a phone, and the customer continues on whichever channel they prefer.

features.d: Order through the website, the mobile app or the Telegram bot, with the same account and cart.
Approve orders, add products and view analytics from a phone.
Apple Pay, Google Pay and Web3 / cryptocurrency integration.
Search products, add them to the cart and track order status inside the chat.
User behaviour, search history and logs analysed for marketing.

architecture.d: Financial transactions and stock in MSSQL with ACID; thousands of clicks and logs per second written asynchronously to MongoDB.
Web, mobile, bot and admin panels talk through one API, so a stock change appears on every channel instantly.

name: PARKHUB
line: A unified smart parking and payment ecosystem
headline: A unified smart parking and payment ecosystem
subtitle: City parking, subscriptions and payments in one app.
chips: ACL isolation through an anti-corruption layer
MCP a custom architecture analysis tool
overview: ParkHub is a mobile platform that digitises city parking infrastructure and automates payments. Users find the nearest zone with geolocation, manage parking sessions in real time, subscribe and pay online securely.
problem: A city has several parking operators, each with its own system and payment method. Drivers cannot see which zones are free, must pay each operator separately and cannot easily track when their parking expires.
approach: The external operators (ParkZone and Axsis) and the EPoint payment gateway sit behind an Anti-Corruption Layer, so their data models never leak into the core domain. The backend uses Clean Architecture, FastEndpoints and MediatR for CQRS, and a custom MCP server automatically checks for architecture drift.
result: Drivers see every operator’s zones in one app, pay with a single subscription and watch their session’s end time live.

features.d: The nearest parking zones on an interactive map.
Start time, elapsed duration and expiry warnings.
One citywide subscription covers payments across all operators.
Reads vehicle plate numbers from the camera using ML Kit.
Centralised Firebase alerts about sessions, payments and subscriptions.

architecture.d: Isolates every interaction with ParkZone, Axsis and EPoint from the internal domain.
A TypeScript Model Context Protocol server maps the codebase’s dependency graph and scores Clean Architecture compliance.
Scheduled jobs and a centralised push-notification system built on Firebase.
